title: SEBI scheme categories and the riskometer
objectives: Name the main SEBI scheme groups and what large, mid and small cap mean.
Read the six levels of the riskometer.
Match a scheme's riskometer to a client's profile.
body_md:
SEBI groups every scheme into a standard category so clients can compare like with like. The main groups are **equity**, **debt**, **hybrid**, **solution-oriented** (retirement, children's) and **other** (index funds, ETFs, funds of funds). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: category count and names change with SEBI circulars; confirm the current list. -->

## Market-cap categories in equity

| Category | Invests mainly in | Minimum equity allocation |
|---|---|---|
| Large cap | Top 100 companies by market cap | 80% in large caps |
| Mid cap | Companies ranked 101 to 250 | 65% in mid caps |
| Small cap | Companies ranked 251 onwards | 65% in small caps |
| Multi cap | All three segments | At least 25% each in large, mid and small |
| Flexi cap | Any market cap, manager's choice | At least 65% in equity |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: minimum allocations and market-cap ranking rules per the latest SEBI categorisation circular and AMFI list. -->

## The riskometer

Every scheme shows a **riskometer** with six levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: the riskometer has six levels since 2020, with the AMC reviewing it monthly; confirm the current rule. --> The level depends on the securities held, not on past returns. It can change when the portfolio changes, so check it at every review.

Debt schemes also carry a **Potential Risk Class** grid, which combines interest-rate risk and credit risk.

## Using it with clients

Match each scheme's riskometer to the client's profile. Never recommend a scheme whose risk level is above the level the client can accept. A mid-cap fund is "Very High" risk even when last year's return looks calm.

> **Investor takeaway:** Read the category and the riskometer before the return figure.
example: A 62-year-old retired client with a Moderate risk profile asks about a small-cap fund that returned 45% last year. The fund's riskometer shows Very High. You decline to recommend it and show categories at or below the client's Moderate level.
say: Every scheme carries a riskometer. Let's match it to what you are comfortable with.
Large, mid and small cap refer to the size of the companies the fund invests in.
never: A small-cap fund is safe because it did well last year.
The riskometer does not matter if the return is good.

check.q: How many levels does the SEBI riskometer show?
check.why: The riskometer has six levels, from Low to Very High.

check.q: A client's profile is Moderate. A scheme's riskometer shows Very High. What should you do?
o: Recommend it, because past returns are strong
Not recommend it, as it exceeds the client's risk level
Ask the client to sign a waiver
check.why: Never recommend a scheme whose risk level exceeds the client's profile.

check.q: In SEBI's categorisation, which segment does a 'mid cap' fund mainly invest in?
check.why: Mid caps are the companies ranked 101 to 250 by market capitalisation.
